svg.text: EchoVault (v4) — HPKE End-to-End Channel · ALICE (browser) ⇄ BOB (echo server) · inside TLS 1.3
Every key is labelled in plain English so you can follow WHO holds it and WHAT crosses the wire. Read the cheat-sheet once, then the stages.
Suite: DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA-256) · KDF: HKDF-SHA-256 · AEAD: ChaCha20-Poly1305
Alice / browser
Bob / echo server
HPKE crypto action
outer TLS 1.3 wrap
attacker @ mitmproxy
KEY CHEAT-SHEET — the whole protocol is just these keys
RULE: SEAL → recipient’s PUBLIC lock · OPEN → your OWN PRIVATE key
ALICE (browser)
BOB (echo server)

text.tspan: = Alice’s PUBLIC lock — Bob seals the reply INTO it
= Bob’s PUBLIC lock — Alice seals the prompt INTO it
= Alice’s PRIVATE key — only Alice OPENS the reply
= Bob’s PRIVATE key — only Bob OPENS the prompt
= Alice’s sign / ID-check keys (prove the lock is hers)
= Bob’s sign / ID-check keys (Alice PINS pkB_ed25519)
= a FRESH throwaway keypair made for EVERY message; skE is destroyed after → forward secrecy

svg.text: GOLDEN RULE: to SEAL, lock with the RECIPIENT’S PUBLIC lock · to OPEN, unlock with YOUR OWN PRIVATE key
STAGE 0
Identity from BIP-39 (done once, offline — private keys NEVER leave the endpoint)
ALICE · derive identity in the browser
256-bit entropy
24-word BIP-39 mnemonic (+ checksum word)
↓ PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 (2048×)
512-bit seed
↓ HKDF-SHA-256 tree (domain-separated)
skA_x25519 / pkA_x25519 ← HPKE keypair
↳ Alice’s PRIVATE key / PUBLIC lock — opens Bob’s replies
skA_ed25519 / pkA_ed25519 ← signing keypair
↳ Alice’s signing key / ID-check key
imported NON-EXTRACTABLE · private keys never sent
BOB · static server identity
static X25519 recipient keypair:
skB_x25519 / pkB_x25519 ← HPKE keypair
↳ Bob’s PRIVATE key / PUBLIC lock — opens Alice’s prompts
static Ed25519 signing keypair:
skB_ed25519 / pkB_ed25519 ← signing keypair
↳ Bob’s signing key / ID-check key
↓ published at GET /pubkey (public-directory stand-in)
↳ serves pkB_x25519 + pkB_ed25519 (+ self-signature)
Alice PINS pkB_ed25519 ⇒ a swapped key is rejected
(only PUBLIC keys are ever published)
STAGE 1
Authenticated handshake (only PUBLIC keys cross the wire — each is Ed25519-signed; Bob’s key is pinned)
= Alice’s PUBLIC lock + Alice’s ID-check key, signed
= Bob’s PUBLIC lock + Bob’s ID-check key, signed (Alice PINS it)
Each side verifies the other’s Ed25519 signature. Swap a key on the wire ⇒ signature check FAILS (T11 / P8).
STAGE 2
Compose (Chat UI) — m = the plaintext prompt we are about to seal
💬 Chat UI · user types a prompt
m = “Summarize patient note #4471 for Dr. Lee…”
m = the cleartext the user typed; nobody but Bob should read it
STAGE 3
HPKE Seal (Alice → Bob) — lock the prompt INTO Bob’s PUBLIC lock
ALICE · Seal( pkB_x25519 , info, aad, m )
SEAL TO → pkB_x25519 (Bob’s PUBLIC lock) OUT: { enc, ct }
1) make a one-time THROWAWAY keypair (skE, pkE)
↳ enc = pkE — throwaway PUBLIC key, travels with the message
2) DH = X25519( skE , pkB_x25519 ) → shared secret
↳ throwaway PRIVATE × Bob’s PUBLIC lock
3) HKDF-SHA-256(DH, info=“echovault/v4”) → K , N0
↳ K = message key, N0 = nonce (Bob derives the SAME two)
4) ct = ChaCha20Poly1305.Seal(K, N0, aad, m)
↳ aad = “echovault/v4” ∥ dir=“c2s” ∥ seq(8B BE)
5) envelope = { enc , ct } ← the only thing that ships
↳ enc = throwaway public key, ct = the locked prompt
6) destroy skE ⇒ per-message forward secrecy
STAGE 4
Transmit client → server (the sealed envelope rides inside the TLS tunnel)
outer TLS 1.3 (wss://) — terminates at the proxy
mitmproxy
TLS terminates
{ enc, ct }
attacker sees only { enc, ct } = ▓▓▓ ciphertext · no skB_x25519 (Bob’s PRIVATE key) ⇒ cannot open
STAGE 5
HPKE Open (Bob) — unlock with Bob’s PRIVATE key, recover the prompt
BOB · Open( enc, skB_x25519 , info, aad, ct )
OPEN WITH → skB_x25519 (Bob’s PRIVATE key — only Bob has it)
1) DH = X25519( skB_x25519 , enc ) → SAME secret
↳ Bob’s PRIVATE key × throwaway PUBLIC key = identical DH
2) HKDF → identical K , N0
3) m = ChaCha20Poly1305.Open(K, N0, aad, ct)
↳ AEAD tag + AAD verified (tamper / replay ⇒ fails closed)
4) recovered prompt m ✓ (Bob is the intended reader)
STAGE 6
Echo + HPKE Seal (Bob → Alice) — lock the reply INTO Alice’s PUBLIC lock
BOB · Seal( pkA_x25519 , info', aad', r )
SEAL TO → pkA_x25519 (Alice’s PUBLIC lock) OUT: { enc', ct' }
1) r = “ECHO: ” + m
2) new THROWAWAY keypair (skE', pkE'); enc' = pkE'
3) DH' = X25519( skE' , pkA_x25519 ) → shared secret
↳ throwaway PRIVATE × Alice’s PUBLIC lock
4) HKDF(DH', info=“echovault/v4”) → K' , N0'
5) ct' = ChaCha20Poly1305.Seal(K', N0', aad', r)
↳ aad' = “echovault/v4” ∥ dir=“s2c” ∥ seq(8B BE)
6) envelope' = { enc' , ct' } ← sealed to Alice
STAGE 7
Transmit server → client (sealed reply, again inside TLS)
outer TLS 1.3 (wss://) — terminates at the proxy
mitmproxy
TLS terminates
{ enc', ct' }
attacker still sees only { enc', ct' } = ▓▓▓ ciphertext · no skA_x25519 (Alice’s PRIVATE key) ⇒ cannot open
STAGE 8
HPKE Open + render (Alice) — unlock with Alice’s PRIVATE key, close the loop
ALICE · Open( enc', skA_x25519 , info', aad', ct' )
OPEN WITH → skA_x25519 (Alice’s PRIVATE key — only Alice has it)
1) DH' = X25519( skA_x25519 , enc' ) → SAME secret
2) HKDF → K' , N0'
3) r = ChaCha20Poly1305.Open(K', N0', aad', ct') ✓
4) 💬 Chat UI renders:
↳ “ECHO: Summarize patient note #4471 for Dr. Lee…”
Why it holds (v4):
Outer TLS protects transport + metadata but TERMINATES at the proxy. The inner HPKE seal protects the payload END-TO-END — only the holder of the recipient’s
PRIVATE X25519 key can Open it: skB_x25519 opens the prompt (Alice → Bob), skA_x25519 opens the reply (Bob → Alice). Everyone in between sees only { enc, ct }.
The handshake is Ed25519-authenticated against a PINNED key (pkB_ed25519), so a swapped /pubkey key is rejected (T11 / P8).
Caveat: Alice’s recipient key (skA/pkA_x25519) is her STATIC BIP-39 key ⇒ the s2c direction has no forward secrecy (→ Morphex epoch-ratchet stretch). Open gap: served-JS.
